title: Runtime selection logic for hardware tuning profile pack (startup + per-model load) and override precedence
creator: Talia Benson
project: Hardware tuning profiles pack (Serving Runtime Performance — Kernel + Scheduling)
description:
Implement deterministic selection of the hardware tuning profile at runtime startup and on per-model load. Define and enforce override precedence across Hosted/Dedicated/Private (fleet defaults vs customer pins), with guardrails, clear logs, and test coverage.

Background
We’re shipping a versioned “profile pack” that contains per-SKU tuning defaults (H100/L40S + B200 preview). This ticket is specifically about the selection logic: how the runtime chooses the active profile_id and how/when it can be overridden.

Goals / acceptance criteria
1) Deterministic selection
- Given the same detected hardware + runtime version + profile_pack_version + model metadata, runtime selects the same profile_id every time.
- Selection happens at:
  a) process startup (global defaults / host-level knobs)
  b) per-model load (model-family-specific kernel + scheduler knobs)

2) Explicit precedence rules
- Documented and implemented precedence order for:
  - fleet defaults (Hosted)
  - cluster/dedicated pool defaults (Dedicated)
  - private install values (Private)
  - per-customer pin (Dedicated/Private)
  - emergency kill-switch / rollback (Hosted)
- Conflicts are resolved deterministically; ambiguous or unsafe combinations fail closed (or fall back) with actionable error messages.

3) Compatibility + guardrails
- Selection must enforce compatibility gates: GPU SKU, form factor where relevant (PCIe vs SXM), MIG/no-MIG, driver/CUDA range.
- Unsafe overrides are rejected with structured reason codes (e.g., "PROFILE_INCOMPATIBLE_DRIVER", "HEADROOM_BELOW_MIN", "UNKNOWN_SKU").

4) Observability + debugging
- Runtime logs a single “profile summary” line at startup (profile_pack_version, selected profile_id, detected sku, driver/cuda, mig mode, key knobs).
- Runtime exposes active profile_id + profile_pack_version via /health and debug endpoints.
- Metrics are tagged with profile_id and sku (owned by ENG-4931 but selection must plumb the values).

Non-goals
- Designing the schema itself (ENG-4922).
- Creating new kernel implementations (covered in kernel/scheduler tickets).

Implementation plan
A) Inputs to selection
- Hardware detection (runtime):
  - sku: H100 | L40S | B200
  - mig_enabled: true/false
  - driver_version
  - cuda_runtime_version
  - device_count / per-device memory
  - optional: interconnect hints (NVLink presence) if we can reliably detect
- Control-plane/runtime config inputs:
  - profile_pack_version (optional, default = runtime-shipped pack version)
  - profile_id (optional explicit pin; only allowed in Dedicated/Private; guarded)
  - feature flag: enable_profile_pack_defaults (Hosted kill-switch)
  - “allow_unsafe_profile_override” must NOT exist (we should not create an easy footgun)

B) Selection algorithm (high level)
1. Load profile pack artifact for requested profile_pack_version (or embedded default).
2. Determine environment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) from config.
3. Resolve “requested override” values:
  - Hosted:
    - ignore customer-level pins
    - allow fleet-level default profile_id only via controlled flag / rollout config
  - Dedicated/Private:
    - allow explicit profile_pack_version pin
    - allow explicit profile_id pin IF compatible and passes guardrails
4. Select candidate set by compatibility predicate:
  - sku match required
  - driver/cuda within allowed range
  - mig constraints respected
5. Apply tie-breakers:
  - prefer exact driver/cuda match over range
  - prefer “stable” profiles over “preview/experimental”
  - prefer profiles with explicit model family match on per-model load
6. If no compatible profile:
  - H100/L40S: fall back to “baseline-safe” profile for that sku (must exist in pack) OR refuse to start depending on environment:
    - Hosted: refuse to start ONLY if would lead to widespread unknown behavior (e.g., unknown sku). Otherwise start on baseline-safe.
    - Dedicated/Private: warn + start on baseline-safe if compatible; refuse if no compatible baseline exists.
  - B200: fail closed unless explicitly pinned to a known-good profile_pack_version that includes B200 support (per project constraint).

C) Per-model load overlay
- Selection returns:
  - global_profile (host defaults)
  - model_profile_overlay (applied when model is loaded)
- Overlay matching keys:
  - model family (e.g., llama, mistral, qwen)
  - quantization mode (fp16/bf16/int8/int4) where relevant
  - context window bucket (short/long) if schema supports it
- If overlay not present: use global defaults.

D) Override precedence (proposed)
Order (highest wins):
1. Emergency rollback flag (Hosted only): disable_profile_pack / revert_to_baseline
2. Explicit profile_id pin (Dedicated/Private only; must pass validation)
3. Explicit profile_pack_version pin (Dedicated/Private)
4. Pool/cluster default profile selection (Dedicated)
5. Fleet default profile selection (Hosted)
6. Embedded runtime defaults (last resort)

Notes:
- We should log whenever an override is applied: source + reason.
- For Dedicated: customer pins must be auditable (PR-24944 is expected to add audit hook; ensure selection returns the resolved values for audit logging).

Test plan
- Unit tests for selection determinism:
  - same inputs => same profile
  - incompatible driver => expected fallback or error
  - unknown sku => error
  - B200 without pin => error
- Golden tests using sample profile pack snapshots (ENG-4922/PR-25037 will add schema validation + snapshots; we should reuse those fixtures).
- Integration tests:
  - start runtime with simulated HW detection matrix (H100 PCIe, H100 SXM if applicable, L40S, MIG on/off)
  - per-model load overlay selection for 2–3 model families

Rollout considerations
- Hosted: selection must support canary cohort gating by environment-configured default profile_id (no customer-level pins).
- Dedicated: default should remain unchanged until customers opt-in; selection must support explicit pin with guardrails.
- Private: selection should be stable given Helm values; should warn loudly if drivers are outside supported range.

Links / related
- Epic: ENG-4921
- Schema + validation: ENG-4922
- Observability tags: ENG-4931
- Related PRs (expected): redwood PR-24881 (selection logic), PR-25014 (/health debug fields), PR-24944 (override + audit)

Open questions
- Do we need to encode “form factor” (PCIe vs SXM) in the compatibility predicate now, or wait until we have a real divergence in knobs?
- For Dedicated, should we allow pinning profile_id without pinning profile_pack_version (i.e., accept “latest pack” + fixed profile_id)? Leaning NO to reduce drift; discuss with Release Eng.
